cosy-lesson.title: The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: activate prior knowledge and introduce key target vocabulary in context.
Concept Check Questions (CCQs): Elicit meaning and drill pronunciation before starting speaking tasks.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review key target vocabulary extracted for this session below:

cosy-vocabulary-item.definition: physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Burnout – physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

p.em: Example: Many employees are suffering from burnout due to long hours.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: rapid 15-minute speaking blitz focused on immediate fluency and target vocabulary usage.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: 15-Min Express Blitz: Share your core opinion on The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition in 90 seconds:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: engage with input reading/listening prompt and launch general topic discussion.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Read/listen to the prompt and discuss the general topic questions:

ol.li:
A: A 4-day work week significantly reduces professional burnout. B: A 5-day week distributes tasks over more days, preventing daily exhaustion.
★ Have you ever suffered from work-related burnout, and how did you recover?

A: Shorter working weeks increase overall productivity because employees waste less time. B: A 5-day week ensures constant availability for clients.
★ Do you feel your personal productivity is higher when you have a structured schedule?

A: An extra day off directly improves mental well-being and reduces stress. B: A standard 5-day routine provides stable habits that support physical health.
★ What activities contribute most to your personal well-being during the weekend?

A: Offering 4-day schedules dramatically boosts staff retention. B: Traditional schedules ensure predictable staffing and corporate stability.
★ Would the promise of a 4-day week influence your choice to stay with a company, affecting employee retention?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: practice comparative analysis and contrasting structures (used to, whereas, compared to).

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Compare the scenario: how it was before vs. now, or life with vs. without it:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: develop stance-taking, opinion justification, and counter-argumentation skills.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Debate these statements. State whether you agree or disagree and justify your position:

ol.li:
A: Compressing 40 hours into 4 days can increase daily burnout and fatigue. B: Working 5 days keeps the daily hours short and manageable.
★ Do you think working 10 hours a day would cause you greater burnout than working 8 hours?

A: A shorter week might harm national productivity in sectors like healthcare. B: Forcing people to work 5 days leads to 'presenteeism' where actual productivity drops.
★ In your opinion, does working longer hours always result in lower productivity?

A: An extra day off might lead to unhealthy habits, reducing overall physical well-being. B: Relentless 5-day schedules leave zero time for self-care and mental well-being.
★ How does a long working week impact your physical and emotional well-being?

A: High employee turnover occurs when 4-day compressed hours harm staff retention. B: Failing to offer modern schedules causes companies to lose talent, destroying long-term retention.
★ Have you ever left a job because the rigid schedule affected your personal life and retention?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative problem solving using modal verbs of recommendation (should, ought to, could).

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Propose practical solutions, actionable advice, and policy recommendations:

ol.li: What are 3 practical steps individuals or organizations should take to address the core challenges of The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition?
What advice would you give to someone experiencing this situation for the first time?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: express future probability and predict long-term developments (is bound to, will likely, is expected to).

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Speculate on future developments and long-term trends:

ol.li: How do you expect The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition to evolve over the next 10 to 20 years?
What unexpected technological or societal changes might reshape this field in the future?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deep-dive case study analysis for 90-min and 120-min lesson formats.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Extended Case Study (90m / 120m format): Analyze this complex real-world scenario:

cosy-blockquote.p: Scenario: An international organization is deciding whether to adopt a mandatory policy regarding The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition. Evaluate the economic, ethical, and social consequences before voting on a final decision.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative group breakout task and synthesis presentation for 120-minute group sessions.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: Group Workshop & Synthesis Presentation (120m Group Format Only): Collaborate and present:

ol.li: In breakout pairs, design a comprehensive action proposal addressing The 4-Day Work Week: Productivity vs. Tradition.
Present your 3-minute synthesis pitch to the full group and defend your recommendations against peer questions.

ul.li: Incorrect: I'm working in this company since 2010 → Correct: I've been working at this company since 2010 ((Present Perfect Continuous))
Incorrect: I suggest to reduce hours → Correct: I suggest reducing hours ((Suggest + -ing))
Incorrect: It is depend on the industry → Correct: It depends on the industry ((Depends as a verb))
Incorrect: The most of employees like it → Correct: Most employees like it ((Generalization))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Summarize main takeaways and review language highlights with your teacher.
